caption_en:
Lebanon, judged like Israel. Ready? 🇱🇧

Same test, same definition: the one Amnesty (2022) and Human Rights Watch (2021) use on Israel. The Rome Statute calls apartheid an "institutionalized regime of systematic oppression and domination". Real facts only:

1. Palestinian refugees have lived in Lebanon since 1948. About 450,000 are registered with UNRWA. They have no Lebanese citizenship.
2. A 2001 law bars them from owning property (Human Rights Watch, 2010).
3. They are barred from over 30 professions, including health care, engineering and law (Amnesty International).
4. Lebanon's side: its constitution rules out the settlement of non-Lebanese, which it says protects the right of return.

By the same definition used on Israel: is this apartheid? You decide.

Israel: about 21% of citizens are Arab. They vote, Arab parties won 19 Knesset seats in October 2026, and Justice Khaled Kabub has sat on the Supreme Court since 2022. Israel has real problems too.

Lebanon is rarely called apartheid. Israel is called it daily. One standard.
caption_he: לבנון, אם היו בודקים אותה כמו את ישראל, לפי אותה הגדרת אפרטהייד שאמנסטי וארגון Human Rights Watch מפעילים על ישראל. עובדות בלבד: פליטים פלסטינים חיים בלבנון מאז 1948, כ-450,000 רשומים באונר"א, ואין להם אזרחות. חוק מ-2001 אוסר עליהם להחזיק ברכוש, ונאסר עליהם לעבוד ביותר מ-30 מקצועות. לבנון אומרת שהחוקה שלה אוסרת יישוב קבע כדי לשמור על זכות השיבה. לפי אותה הגדרה, האם זה אפרטהייד? תחליטו אתם. בישראל כ-21% מהאזרחים ערבים, הם מצביעים, המפלגות הערביות זכו ב-19 מושבים, ושופט ערבי יושב בבית המשפט העליון. גם לישראל יש בעיות אמיתיות. אותו סטנדרט לכולן.

lines.line: The test: the same apartheid definition used on Israel.
Palestinians have lived in Lebanon since 1948. Three generations, born there.
Citizenship? No. Own a home? Since 2001, the law says no. Work as a doctor, lawyer or engineer? Barred from over 30 professions.
Lebanon says its constitution rules out settling them, to protect their right of return.
By the same definition used on Israel: is this apartheid? You decide.
Israel: one in five citizens is Arab. They vote. Arab parties won 19 seats. Arab judges sit on the Supreme Court.
Lebanon is rarely called apartheid. Israel is called it daily. Both have real problems. One standard.
So, let's run the test again.
